text: No well-ordered State ever strikes a balance between the services of its citizens and their misdeeds; but appointing rewards for good actions and punishment for bad, when it has rewarded a man for acting well, will afterwards, should he act ill, chastise him, without regard to his former deserts.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
